builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: STISA: A 0.16 GOPS/W/PE Single-Shot Inference FPGA-based SNN Accelerator with Algorithm and Hardware Co-Design
summary: The method replaces multi-timestep SNN inference and prior SNN accelerator dataflows with Temporal Splitter Compression plus a co-designed FPGA architecture (TPOS mapping and Block-Mux Streaming). It costs FPGA development effort, model conversion into the TSS spiking form, and accuracy risk on harder tasks (ImageNet top-1 of 68.51% trails conventional CNN/Transformer baselines). It can fail if the target workload is not vision with event-driven tolerance, if the team lacks FPGA tooling and HLS/RTL expertise, or if accuracy degradation from timestep compression exceeds the application's threshold.
rationale: The technique targets spiking neural networks on custom FPGA hardware, which is outside the reader's GPU/API production stack and provides no transferable gain for LLM or standard deep-learning workloads.
technique: FPGA SNN accelerator with timestep compression

claims.statement: The method replaces multi-timestep SNN inference and prior SNN accelerator dataflows with Temporal Splitter Compression plus a co-designed FPGA architecture (TPOS mapping and Block-Mux Streaming). It costs FPGA development effort, model conversion into the TSS spiking form, and accuracy risk on harder tasks (ImageNet top-1 of 68.51% trails conventional CNN/Transformer baselines). It can fail if the target workload is not vision with event-driven tolerance, if the team lacks FPGA tooling and HLS/RTL expertise, or if accuracy degradation from timestep compression exceeds the application's threshold.

FPGA prototypes deliver up to 7.99x speedup, 30.4% power reduction, and 30.1% LUT reduction versus prior SNN accelerators, with TSC cutting synaptic operations by 24.44%-51.71% at competitive accuracy (e.g., 68.51% ImageNet, 96.38% CIFAR-10); reported efficiency is 0.16 GOPS/W/PE.
